requirements.note: Inset grouped list with Pinned and Notes sections, newest first; title plus a one-line preview with a short or relative date (time today, weekday this week, otherwise m/d/yy).
Search field under the large title filters by title and body as you type, keeping the Pinned/Notes sections; has a clear button and a Close button.
Tapping a row pushes an editor with title and body text views. Edits save on Back with no Save button and the note moves to the top of its section.
The compose button opens a blank note with the keyboard up. Leaving it empty discards it (count unchanged); a note with text is kept (count 90 to 91).
Swipe right on a row to pin or unpin (a full swipe works), swipe left to delete, and long-press for a context menu with Pin/Unpin Note and Delete.
'90 Notes' appears in the bottom toolbar, like Apple Notes, and updates on create and delete.
The new note, the edits, the pin, unpin and delete all survived a relaunch.

tells: At the largest text size the long title in the editor breaks inside a word ('recommendat / ions').
The note count in the bottom toolbar stays small at the largest text size, while the list text scales.
A.scroll: Native table scrolling: slow drags, flings and the rubber-band past the top all feel right. No blank or popping rows, and the scroll position is kept when you come back from a note.

requirements.note: Inset grouped list with Pinned and Notes sections, newest first; title plus a one-line preview with a short or relative date.
Search field in the bottom toolbar (iOS 26 style) filters by title and body as you type and returns the same results as A.
Tapping a row pushes an editor. Title and body edits save automatically and the note moves to the top, showing 'Today at …'.
The compose button in the nav bar opens a blank note with the keyboard up. An empty note is discarded and a note with text is kept (91 Notes).
Swipe left deletes and long-press gives Pin Note/Delete, but there is no swipe right to pin: the drag opens the note instead. Pin is also in the editor's toolbar.
'90 Notes' subtitle under the large title, updated live.
Created, edited, pinned, unpinned and deleted notes all survived a relaunch.

bugs: Swiping a row to the right opens the note as though it had been tapped, where an iPhone list would do nothing or show leading actions.
tells: No leading swipe action to pin. In Apple Notes and native lists, pin is a leading swipe.
At the largest text size, list rows stay one line and truncate hard ('Podcast rec…', '9/27/26 May…'), where a native cell would wrap and grow.
At the largest text size the long title in the editor breaks inside a word ('recommenda / tions').
Rows show up to accessibility as one Button inside a cell rather than as a cell with its own label and text.
B.scroll: Smooth, native-feeling scrolling with no blank or popping rows. Flings and the rubber-band at the top behave, and the scroll position is kept after visiting a note.

why: Both apps meet nearly the whole spec with a convincing iOS 26 look in light and dark. A also has the leading swipe to pin and list rows that wrap at the largest text size. B has no leading swipe (a right swipe opens the note instead), and its rows truncate to unreadable fragments at the largest text size, so A feels more like a hand-built iPhone app.
